messages.text: Ronaldo breaks silence over Portugal walkout in extraordinary statement

metadata.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo has broken his silence over his Portugal walkout in a lengthy statement in which he declares himself available for the national team.
metadata.content: Cristiano Ronaldo: Portugal star breaks silence over national team walkout in statement | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Breaking Cristiano Ronaldo: Portugal star breaks silence over national team walkout in statement Cristiano Ronaldo delivers on his promise to explain why he walked out on the Portugal camp as he accuses head coach Jorge Jesus of broken promises and apologises to his team-mates and the people of Portugal Tuesday 6 October 2026 21:14, UK Cristiano Ronaldo has broken his silence over his Portugal walkout in a lengthy statement in which he declares himself available for the national team. The 41-year-old, whose actions had raised doubts over his international future, also accused Portugal's new head coach Jorge Jesus of broken promises as he explained his reasons for leaving the camp. Addressing the uncertainty over his Portugal future, the Al Nassr forward said in a statement on Instagram: "If I am physically well, playing for my club, with goals I hope, after serving the suspension that may be applied to me, I will be available, as I have always been until today, to compete and win for our national team." Ronaldo left the national team squad in Copenhagen on the eve of a Nations League fixture against Denmark after he was an unused substitute for a 2-1 win away to Norway on September 27. messages.text: 'FIA to blame for F1's Bahrain GP software farce'

metadata.summary: David Croft has criticised the FIA for the chaotic formation lap scenes at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, describing a software glitch that saw several drivers slowing to a crawl or stopping completely as a "farce".
metadata.content: Bahrain Grand Prix software glitch: FIA to blame for Sepang 'farce', says David Croft | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Opinion Bahrain Grand Prix software glitch: FIA to blame for Sepang 'farce', says David Croft Sky Sports F1's David Croft discusses the chaos caused by a software glitch at the Bahrain Grand Prix, labelling the scenes in Sepang a "farce"; watch F1's first ever Singapore Grand Prix Sprint weekend live on Sky Sports F1, with Sprint Qualifying at 1pm on Friday David Croft Commentator @CroftyF1 Tuesday 6 October 2026 20:12, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen compare the starting procedure issues in Sepang during the Bahrain GP in Malaysia to the F1 Lego race. David Croft has criticised the FIA for the chaotic formation lap scenes at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, describing a software glitch that saw several drivers slowing to a crawl or stopping completely as a "farce". F1 and the FIA have new technical regulations this year which saw the introduction of a new power unit which is almost 50 per cent electric. Sepang saw the first wet conditions of the season, and the FIA later confirmed that a combination of low engine speeds, low grip, wet-weather energy-management settings and the configuration of the circuit had caused an unintended loss of power. Speaking on the F1 Show podcast, Sky Sports F1 commentator Croft questioned why such a scenario had not been simulated before the season

messages.text: Djokovic wins China Open without needing a match point in semi-final and final

metadata.summary: Former world No 1 Novak Djokovic won his seventh China Open title without needing a match point in his semi-final and final.
metadata.content: Novak Djokovic: Former world No 1 wins China Open title without needing a match point in semi-final and final | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Novak Djokovic: Former world No 1 wins China Open title without needing a match point in semi-final and final Novak Djokovic earns his seventh career title in Beijing after Alex De Minaur is forced to retire injured after Daniil Medvedev was defaulted in their semi-final; you can watch the WTA/ATP China Open and ATP 1000 Shanghai Masters live on Sky Sports Tuesday 6 October 2026 14:50, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Alex De Minaur retired in the China Open final against Novak Djokovic after winning a brilliant opening game of the second set Former world No 1 Novak Djokovic won his seventh China Open title without needing a match point in his semi-final and final. Djokovic, who was awarded a win after his semi-final opponent Daniil Medvedev was disqualified after hitting a spectator with the ball , claimed the 102nd title of his career following the retirement of De Minaur in the final. De Minaur, who left the ​court for ⁠a medical ⁠timeout after the first set, ‌continued playing with a heavy bandage on ‌his left thigh. But he could not continue after winning ⁠the first game ​of the second ​set. Djokovic narrowly won ​the first set, ⁠with the match poised at ⁠7-6 (7-3) 0-1 when ​De Minaur retired. metadata.summary: Carlos Alcaraz has won his first final since coming back from a long injury lay-off for a right wrist injury with success at the Japan Open.
metadata.content: Carlos Alcaraz: Spaniard wins Japan Open in first final since coming back from injury lay-off for wrist injury | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Carlos Alcaraz: Spaniard wins Japan Open in first final since coming back from injury lay-off for wrist injury Carlos Alcaraz successfully defends Japan Open title in his first final since suffering wrist injury which forced him to miss French Open and Wimbledon; you can watch the ATP 1000 Shanghai Masters live on Sky Sports from Wednesday Tuesday 6 October 2026 14:55, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Carlos Alcaraz against Jiri Lehecka from the Japan Open final Carlos Alcaraz has won his first final since coming back from a long injury lay-off for a right wrist injury with success at the Japan Open. Alcaraz, who hadn't played a showpiece since getting beat by Jannik Sinner at the Monte-Carlo Masters in April successfully defended the title he won last year in Tokyo defeating Jiri Lehecka 7-6 (7-4) 6-4. The Spaniard returned from injury in late August and made a run to the US Open quarter-finals, where he lost to Ben Shelton in a match that ended at 3:33am . Russell suffered a power unit failure late in Sunday's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia when running third, forcing him to retire while his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli finished second to extend his lead over the Brit at the top of the Drivers' Championship to 84 points with seven rounds remaining. Sky Sports News understands Russell will take on a new power unit on Friday in Singapore, which will see him exceed the season allocation of four for each driver, therefore incurring a penalty that will drop him to the rear of the grid.
